clue: Sorting patients by urgency of need for care
rationale: Triage prioritizes by acuity and threat to life, not arrival time.

clue: Swelling caused by fluid trapped in body tissues
rationale: Document location, symmetry, and pitting; sudden unilateral swelling warrants prompt assessment.

clue: Deficiency of red blood cells or hemoglobin
rationale: Low oxygen-carrying capacity can cause fatigue, dyspnea, tachycardia, and pallor.
Suspect sepsis with infection plus organ dysfunction; obtain cultures and give prescribed antimicrobials promptly.
Persistent emesis raises aspiration, dehydration, electrolyte, and acid-base concerns.

clue: Understanding a patient's feelings, not just their chart
rationale: Therapeutic communication validates the patient's experience without giving false reassurance.

clue: Temporary loss of consciousness from reduced blood flow to the brain
rationale: Protect from injury, assess airway and vitals, and investigate potential cardiac or neurologic causes.
Check mucous membranes and nail beds too; pallor can signal poor perfusion or anemia.
Afebrile does not rule out infection, especially in older or immunocompromised patients.
New dyspnea is an ABC priority: assess work of breathing, oxygenation, and lung sounds immediately.

clue: Absence of harmful microorganisms in care technique
rationale: Breaks in sterile technique require correction before continuing an invasive procedure.
A STAT order takes priority; clarify anything unclear rather than delaying a time-sensitive intervention.

clue: Temp, pulse, respiration, and blood pressure, collectively
rationale: Trends matter more than one value; compare findings with the patient's baseline and clinical picture.
Verify which medications may still be given and assess aspiration risk before any oral intake.
